claims.text: Furnace annealing of atmospheric plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coatings on SS316L promotes interdiffusion at the coating-substrate interface.
Furnace annealing promotes interdiffusion within the AlCoCrFeNi coating.
Annealing promotes phase homogenization in the coating.
Annealing improves coating cohesion and the coating-substrate interfacial microstructure.
Annealing produces a dense and uniform passive oxide layer.
Annealing-induced interdiffusion promotes the formation of stable oxide phases.
The stable oxide phases impede oxygen penetration into the SS316L substrate.
The stable oxide phases impede corrosive-ion penetration into the SS316L substrate.
The dense, uniform passive oxide barrier enhances the corrosion resistance of coated SS316L.
Annealed, coated SS316L will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than both bare SS316L and non-annealed coated SS316L under the same exposure conditions.
Annealed, coated SS316L will exhibit less pitting than both bare SS316L and non-annealed coated SS316L.
Annealed, coated SS316L will exhibit less material loss than both bare SS316L and non-annealed coated SS316L.
The proposed mechanism applies in chemical-processing and nuclear-power corrosion environments where chemical or diffusion-controlled corrosion dominates.
The proposed protection mechanism may not apply when failure is dominated by mechanical wear or extreme thermomechanical stress.
The magnitude of corrosion-resistance improvement depends on the annealing parameters.
The composition and uniformity of the oxide layer depend on the annealing parameters and initial coating microstructure.
The controlled study will compare annealed coated, non-annealed coated, and uncoated SS316L under the same aggressive environment.
A lack of statistically significant corrosion improvement and protective oxide formation in the annealed group would falsify the proposed annealing-induced passive-barrier mechanism.
